quotes.text: It’s unlikely your business needs to create a custom mandate agreement.
After your customer accepts the mandate agreement, you can immediately debit the first payment due from your customer’s account.
Pre-notifications are required if not expressly waived.

findings: The new-versus-old raw delta is presentational table normalization, a Stripe API link parameter selecting direct-api, and an http-to-https Stripe example link; no changed PAD requirement or new guarantee was found (diff lines 3-59; old lines 28, 39-74; new lines 29, 40-72).

The mapped source line 21 calls the table '9 required elements' but enumerates 11 entries at lines 23-33. The new raw has 11 requirement rows at lines 41-72; two rows are explicitly conditional on payment_schedule (new lines 56-64). Correct the count and conditional label in source, and the same '9 required elements' route labels in wiki/stripe-index.md line 255 and wiki/concepts/stripe-acss-debit.md line 113. This is an existing-source correction, separate from the raw delta.

Source line 30 compresses the pre-notification rule into a waiver condition. Keep the precise distinction that pre-notifications are required unless expressly waived, and any opt-out waiver text must be bold, highlighted, or underlined (new lines 66-69; old lines 67-71).

The example thirty-day cancellation notice and Rocket Rides contact information are sample terms, not universal mandated values (new lines 41-51, 71). The recourse statement is required verbatim in its entirety (new line 70).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The 2026-05-02 capture already states that a custom agreement is unusual, identifies the two use cases, and says custom emails and schedule terms alone do not require one (old lines 6-22; new lines 7-23).

Both captures require acceptance and confirmation terms for immediate debit and confirmation within five days, with pre-debit notice unless modified or expressly waived (old lines 30-32, 66-71; new lines 31-33, 65-69).

Both captures condition payment-schedule/triggers and sporadic authorization rows on mandate payment_schedule values and require the recourse statement, cancellation terms, and Stripe PSP disclosure (old lines 56-74; new lines 56-72).
conflicts: Existing source line 21 and the Stripe index/concept route labels say 9 required elements, while the source itself lists 11 and the captured table has 11 rows, including conditional schedule rows.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit/custom-pad-agreement, the 2026-11-07 capture retains the prior PAD mandate guidance: a custom agreement is uncommon, and the schedule and sporadic-authorization rows apply only to their specified `payment_schedule` values (new lines 7, 56-64; old lines 6, 56-65). The mapped [[source-stripe-acss-custom-pad-agreement]] therefore needs a count and conditional-label correction, while the raw-to-raw change itself is formatting and link selection, not a new mandate rule.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit/custom-pad-agreement, [[source-stripe-acss-custom-pad-agreement]] should preserve that pre-debit notices remain required unless expressly waived, and waiver wording has visual-emphasis requirements (new lines 66-69; old lines 67-71). It should also distinguish the sample thirty-day notice and Rocket Rides details from universal rules, and retain the exact recourse-text obligation (new lines 70-72; old lines 72-74). The current '9 required elements' label conflicts with its own 11-item list and both captured tables.
